data.name: Mary
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew Mariam meaning 'rebellion' or 'bitterness', derived from the root marah, meaning 'to be bitter'. In the Bible, Mary is the mother of Jesus and a central figure in Christian faith. She is revered as a saint and a model of faith and obedience.

in_hebrew.name: מריה
in_hebrew.meaning: מילה שפירושה מר של עשבים מרירים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם מריה נגזר מהמילה העברית מר, שפירושה מר או מרה, ויכול להתייחס לעשבים מרירים או למרירות. השם מריה משויך לאמו של ישו, מרים, ומשקף את חשיבותה וקדושתה בתרבות היהודית והנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Μαρία
in_greek.meaning: το όνομα που σημαίνει πικρή ή επιθυμητή
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μαρία προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή λέξη 'מר', που σημαίνει πικρή ή επιθυμητή. Στο Ευαγγέλιο, η Μαρία είναι η μητέρα του Ιησού και η ονομασία της συνδέεται με την πικρή και τη λύπη, αλλά και με την ελπίδα και τη σωτηρία.

in_latin.name: Maria
in_latin.meaning: name meaning bitter or wished-for child
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Maria is derived from the Hebrew word 'מר', meaning bitter or wished-for child. In Christian tradition, Maria refers to the mother of Jesus, embodying virtues of faith, hope, and charity. The name has been revered in Latin-speaking cultures, symbolizing spiritual purity and devotion.

in_english.name: Mary
in_english.meaning: bitter or beloved, a wished-for child
in_english.long_meaning: The name Mary originates from the Hebrew 'מר', meaning bitter or beloved. In Christianity, Mary is the mother of Jesus, representing faith, humility, and devotion. The name has been a timeless classic across cultures, symbolizing spiritual significance, purity, and maternal love.

biblical_reference.note: The name Mary is prominently featured in the New Testament as the mother of Jesus.

saint_reference.note: The Blessed Virgin Mary is venerated in the Catholic Church and other Christian denominations.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mary is one of the most popular given names for girls around the world. It is the name of the beloved mother of Jesus and a symbol of motherhood, playing an essential role in Christian tradition and art. Many cathedrals, shrines, and churches are dedicated to Mary, and her image graces countless works of art, reflecting the importance of the maternal figure in religious and cultural contexts.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian faith, Mary is an embodiment of humility, obedience, and strength. She is an ideal of faith and devotion, and her story inspires countless saints and religious figures throughout history. Believers pray to her for intercession and guidance, and many believe that she holds a special place in the hearts of God and Jesus. In her role as the mother of Jesus, Mary provides a bridge between God and humanity and offers comfort, hope, and inspiration to believers.

historical_references.context: The Catholic Church defines the dogma that Mary, the mother of Jesus, was assumed into heaven at the end of her earthly life.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern times, the Christian name 'Mary' has seen a resurgence in various contexts beyond traditional religious practices. Among the trends are increased devotion and spirituality, with many individuals seeking to connect deeply with the figure of Mary through prayer and meditation. Additionally, there is an emerging trend towards feminist interpretations of Mary, viewing her as a strong and independent woman who has influenced the role of women in society and religion. These trends can be observed across multiple platforms, including social media where people share their personal experiences and beliefs, religious websites where communities form around specific interpretations of Mary, and podcasts where scholars and theologians discuss contemporary perspectives on Mary's role in Christianity.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Mary, in Christian tradition, represents the embodiment of purity, humility, and devotion. Her name, derived from the Hebrew Miriam, signifies bitterness turned sweet, reflecting her role as the Mother of God and the suffering servant.
